datasets.name: MIMIC-IV
datasets.verdict_rationale: Usable as the patient-linked core, conditional on two things that are not yet done: completed CITI training and granted PhysioNet credentialing (TASK-0011), and signing the DUA, which only a human may do. Its licence forbids redistribution and limits use to scientific research, so it constrains what may be released, not only what may be trained.

license.name: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0
license.notes: Licence text read at source: 'The LICENSEE will not share access to PhysioNet restricted data with anyone else'; use is limited to 'lawful use in scientific research and no other'; re-identification is forbidden; code behind publications must be contributed to an open repository. The licence addresses the data, not model weights derived from it, so open-weight compatibility is genuinely UNKNOWN and must be settled with PhysioNet in writing before any release. It must not be assumed permissible.

access.mechanism: PhysioNet credentialed access: credentialing application, CITI training, then signing the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0
access.notes: CITI requirement read at source: course 'Data or Specimens Only Research', affiliation 'Massachusetts Institute of Technology Affiliates' (the option provided for non-MIT personnel), and the application must carry the training REPORT, not the certificate. Registering as an independent learner incurs fees and is advised against. This is the concrete dependency on TASK-0011.

patient_linkage.notes: subject_id is stable and, per the MIMIC-CXR documentation, denotes the same individuals in MIMIC-IV v2.2 and later. This is the only genuine patient-level cross-modality link available among all seven candidates.

temporal_validity.derivation_if_absent: Use storetime, not charttime, as available_at_time. charttime records when the observation was made (specimen collection); storetime records when the result became available or was validated in the system. A clinician cannot act on a lab result at collection time, so deriving available_at_time from charttime would leak future information into the decision snapshot. Note the known data-quality caveat that a non-trivial share of chartevents rows carry charttime > storetime, so the derivation needs an explicit rule for inconsistent pairs.
temporal_validity.notes: PARTIAL, not YES: the dataset carries timestamps that support a correct derivation, but it does not itself publish an availability time.

care_setting.setting: Inpatient hospital admission and ICU stay
care_setting.population: Adults admitted to a single US tertiary academic medical centre; the surveyed evidence covers the hosp and icu modules
care_setting.notes: VERIFIED against this record's own evidence, which names the hosp and icu modules and nothing else. The MIMIC-IV ED module was never surveyed and is not part of this record, so DS-0001 as surveyed cannot supply a triage-point snapshot: it has no first-contact chief complaint and no triage note. This is the direct basis of RISK-0014. Closing the gap requires MIMIC-IV-ED as DS-0008 (TASK-0031), not a re-reading of this record.

use_restrictions: no redistribution or sharing of access
publication code must be contributed to an open repository
obligations.notes: External transfer prohibited by the licence and independently by DEC-0006. No evidence item may reach an external provider.

evidence: https://physionet.org/content/mimiciv/ — version 3.1, credentialed access, licence name, hosp and icu modules
https://physionet.org/about/licenses/physionet-credentialed-health-data-license-150/ — redistribution, commercial use and re-identification restrictions
https://physionet.org/about/citi-course/ — required CITI course, affiliation option, and training-report requirement
https://github.com/MIT-LCP/mimic-iv-website/blob/master/content/hosp/labevents.md — charttime and storetime semantics
https://github.com/MIT-LCP/mimic-code/issues/1657 — known charttime > storetime inconsistency

datasets.name: MIMIC-CXR
datasets.verdict_rationale: Same conditions as MIMIC-IV, and valuable for the same reason: it is the half of the patient-linked core that supplies 2D imaging and radiology reports for patients who also appear in MIMIC-IV.

license.name: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0
license.notes: Same licence and the same unresolved model-release question as DS-0001.

access.mechanism: PhysioNet credentialed access with CITI training and a signed Data Use Agreement
access.notes: The DUA additionally forbids sharing the data, attempting re-identification, and publishing without releasing associated code.

patient_linkage.notes: subject_id values (range 10,000,000-19,999,999) represent the same individuals as in MIMIC-IV v2.2 and later, which is what makes a single-patient multimodal journey possible at all.

temporal_validity.derivation_if_absent: Study and report timestamps must be mapped onto the MIMIC-IV timeline; the report becomes available only when authored, not when the image was acquired. The two must not be collapsed.
temporal_validity.notes: The linkage and licence were read at source; the exact timestamp columns were not. Must be confirmed against the MIMIC-CXR table documentation before any snapshot is built.

care_setting.setting: Radiology archive attached to the MIMIC hospital cohort
care_setting.population: Patients of the same institution as DS-0001, linkable by subject_id
care_setting.notes: The survey recorded DICOM images plus free-text reports and never recorded which encounters the studies come from. Whether the archive is emergency, inpatient or mixed is unestablished, so no claim may rest on its covering the evaluated triage setting. Resolving this is part of TASK-0031, since a chest film ordered at triage and one ordered on the ward are different evidence at the same decision moment.

evidence: https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/ — licence, credentialed access, subject_id linkage to MIMIC-IV, DICOM images plus free-text reports
https://physionet.org/about/licenses/physionet-credentialed-health-data-license-150/ — licence restrictions

datasets.name: CheXpert
datasets.verdict_rationale: Usable only as an unlinked capability subset for 2D chest imaging. It shares no patient identifier with the MIMIC core, so it cannot contribute to a single-patient multimodal journey. Condition: read and accept the Stanford Research Use Agreement at registration, and confirm what it permits for released model weights.

license.name: Stanford University Dataset Research Use Agreement
license.notes: Secondary sources agree the RUA restricts use to non-commercial research and forbids distributing, publishing or reproducing a copy of the dataset. The agreement text itself was not retrieved, so this is recorded UNVERIFIED rather than upgraded on agreement between second-hand summaries.

access.mechanism: Request through Stanford AIMI Shared Datasets; acceptance of the Research Use Agreement
access.notes: citi_required set False because the provider is Stanford AIMI, not PhysioNet; to be confirmed at registration.

patient_linkage.notes: A separate patient population from MIMIC. Whatever internal identifier exists, it cannot be joined to subject_id.

temporal_validity.derivation_if_absent: No clinical timeline is expected; if confirmed absent, this dataset can support imaging capability but not time-valid decision snapshots.

care_setting.population: A separate patient population from the MIMIC family; the collecting department is not recorded
care_setting.notes: The setting was never recorded by the survey and is not derivable from the evidence held. Irrespective of setting, this record is already linkable_across_modalities NO with no clinical timeline, so it can only ever be unlinked capability evidence and never journey evidence for any setting.

evidence: https://stanfordaimi.azurewebsites.net/datasets/8cbd9ed4-2eb9-4565-affc-111cf4f7ebe2 — dataset landing page (licence text not exposed without registration)
https://github.com/sfu-db/covid19-datasets/blob/master/datasets-details/stanford-chexpert.md — secondary summary of the Research Use Agreement terms
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.03020 — datasheet for CheXpert, secondary description of use restrictions

datasets.name: BraTS (Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge)
datasets.verdict_rationale: Provides 3D MRI capability only, and only for brain tumour imaging. It is a separate population, heavily preprocessed, and carries no clinical timeline, so it cannot support a time-valid decision snapshot. It does not satisfy the submitted document's 3D CT claim. Condition: accept it as an unlinked 3D MRI capability subset and say so plainly in the Proposal.

license.name: BraTS challenge data-use agreement
license.notes: Secondary sources describe a data-use agreement permitting academic, non-commercial research use and requiring citation of the BraTS challenge papers. Terms differ by challenge year; the specific year used must have its own record.

access.mechanism: Registration through the Synapse portal for the relevant challenge year

patient_linkage.notes: Separate population from MIMIC; no join is possible.

temporal_validity.derivation_if_absent: None available. Volumes are supplied skull-stripped, co-registered to the SRI24 atlas and resampled to 1mm isotropic, i.e. as a preprocessed segmentation benchmark rather than as a clinical record. There is no acquisition or result-availability time to derive from.
temporal_validity.notes: Recorded NO on the strength of the documented preprocessing pipeline; to be confirmed against the challenge data description for the year actually used.

care_setting.notes: VERIFIED against this record's own evidence, which states the data is supplied skull-stripped, co-registered to the SRI24 atlas and resampled to 1mm isotropic, that is, as a preprocessed segmentation benchmark rather than as a clinical record. There is no care episode and no acquisition time to attach a decision moment to.

use_restrictions: citation of the BraTS challenge papers required

evidence: https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn53708249/wiki/627759 — BraTS 2024 challenge portal (terms not retrievable without registration)
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11945730/ — review of BraTS datasets 2012-2025, modalities and preprocessing
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.09310 — T1, T1ce, T2 and FLAIR sequences; skull-stripping, co-registration and 1mm isotropic resampling

datasets.name: VQA-RAD
datasets.verdict_rationale: The least encumbered candidate and the only one reported as fully permissive. It is an evaluation benchmark of 2,248 question-answer pairs over 315 images, not a patient record set, so it supports a VQA-style evaluation task and nothing about patient journeys. Condition: confirm the CC0 declaration at the OSF source.

license.name: CC0 1.0 Universal
license.notes: Reported as CC0 1.0 by secondary sources including the Hugging Face mirror. If confirmed at the OSF source, this is the one candidate that places no constraint on an open-weight release.

access.mechanism: Open download from OSF; also mirrored on Hugging Face

patient_linkage.notes: Built from MedPix teaching images; there is no patient cohort to link.

temporal_validity.derivation_if_absent: None. This is a question-answering benchmark with no clinical timeline; it can only serve as an evaluation task, never as a decision snapshot.

care_setting.population: MedPix teaching-file images; no patient cohort exists
care_setting.notes: VERIFIED against this record's own evidence: built from MedPix teaching images, with no patient cohort to link. It supports a question-answering evaluation task and nothing about patient journeys in any setting.

obligations.notes: external_transfer_permitted left UNKNOWN deliberately: a permissive licence does not by itself authorise sending content to an external provider, which DEC-0006 governs separately.

evidence: https://osf.io/89kps/wiki/home/ — OSF project wiki for VQA-RAD
https://huggingface.co/datasets/flaviagiammarino/vqa-rad — mirror stating CC0 1.0 Universal; 2,248 QA pairs over 315 images, built from MedPix
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30457565/ — source publication

datasets.name: SLAKE
datasets.verdict_rationale: A bilingual VQA benchmark of 642 images and 14,028 question-answer pairs. Condition: the licence is genuinely ambiguous across sources and must be resolved at the project page before use, because the difference between CC BY-SA and CC BY-NC-SA decides whether it constrains the release.

license.name: AMBIGUOUS: reported as CC BY-SA 4.0 by some sources and CC BY-NC-SA by others
license.notes: This ambiguity is the reason the dataset stays CONDITIONAL. A ShareAlike term propagates to derivative works and a NonCommercial term restricts them; the two readings have materially different consequences for an open-weight release and cannot be averaged.

access.mechanism: Download from the project page; also mirrored on Hugging Face

care_setting.population: Bilingual visual question-answering benchmark over 642 images; no patient cohort
care_setting.notes: The absence of a care setting follows from the record holding no patient identifier, no linkage and no temporal structure, but the survey never read a source statement on provenance, so this stays UNVERIFIED. The licence ambiguity on this record is unresolved and is the more urgent question.

evidence: http://www.med-vqa.com/slake — project page named as the licence source of record
https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09542 — source publication; 642 images and 14,028 QA pairs, bilingual English/Chinese
https://huggingface.co/datasets/Voxel51/SLAKE — mirror; licence statements across mirrors disagree

datasets.name: CT-RATE
datasets.verdict_rationale: Added on 2026-08-30 to cover the 3D CT modality the submitted Project Idea claims and no other candidate supplies. It is the dataset behind Hamamci et al. (2026), which the submitted document already cites. Condition: its CC-BY-NC-SA licence is NonCommercial and ShareAlike, which constrains an open-weight release and must be reconciled with the release plan before it is relied upon.

license.name: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
license.notes: Read at the dataset page: released under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike, permitting non-commercial research use with attribution and requiring derivatives to be shared under similar terms. Recorded open_weight_release_compatible=NO because ShareAlike propagates to derivative works and NonCommercial forbids commercial use, which is incompatible with an unqualified open-weight release. Some listings cite CC-BY-4.0; the dataset page itself states NC-SA and that is what is recorded.

access.mechanism: Hugging Face gated dataset: contact information must be shared and terms accepted before download
access.notes: Accepting the terms is a binding act and must be performed by a human, not an agent.

patient_linkage.notes: Filenames follow split_patientID_scanID_reconstructionID over 21,304 unique patients, so patients can be kept within a single split — which satisfies the patient-level splitting rule internally. The identifier is internal to CT-RATE and cannot be joined to MIMIC subject_id.

temporal_validity.derivation_if_absent: None available. The dataset documents no timestamps and no longitudinal structure, so it cannot support a time-valid decision snapshot and can only serve as a 3D CT capability and evaluation subset.

care_setting.population: 21,304 patients; the collecting department, institution and country are not recorded
care_setting.notes: The survey recorded volume counts and the filename identifier structure but no provenance of care setting. The record already documents no timestamps and no longitudinal structure, so it cannot supply a decision snapshot in the evaluated setting or any other; it is unlinked 3D capability evidence only.

use_restrictions: derivatives must be shared under similar terms (ShareAlike)

evidence: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibrahimhamamci/CT-RATE — CC-BY-NC-SA licence, gated access, 25,692 volumes expanded to 50,188 reconstructions from 21,304 patients, naming structure, no timestamps documented
https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17834 — source publication (Hamamci et al.), cited in the submitted Project Idea
https://github.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CLIP — associated code released under CC-BY-NC-SA
